article_title: Axiomatic quantum mechanics: Necessity and benefits for the physics studies
citation: Jasmina Jeknić-Dugić, Momir Arsenijević, Miroljub Dugić. (2017). Axiomatic quantum mechanics: Necessity and benefits for the physics studies. arXiv preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.00268
title: Teach quantum mechanics axiomatically, using representation-independent Dirac notation and postponing historical visualizations, applications and interpretations.
description: The article's central design principle: present the postulates systematically as "the shortest and most eﬃcie nt path to familiarizing with the basics and universal use of quantum mechanics", keep formulas in representation-independent Dirac form, and defer visualizations and explanations to specialized courses because they "produce the puzzles and make the theory ”myste rious”" before becoming useful.
requirements: Proper student preparation before starting: courses in the classical-mechanics Hamilton formalism, basic statistical physics, theory of probability and a basic course in linear algebra, so the Hilbert and rigged Hilbert space can be smoothly introduced.
constraints: The article acknowledges the full mathematical foundations are demanding and time-consuming for starters, so "some balance is required for the introductory course", and notes neither the outcome nor unique solutions can be expected of finding that balance.
target_learning_goals: understanding the basic postulates and universal formalism of non-relativistic quantum theory
examples: The article derives the electric quadruple-moment expression eq.(6) from the postulates as a worked illustration that "the origin and the meaning of eq.(6) beco mes obvious" without memorization.
